title: Spot price used instead of TWAP allows flash-loan liquidation manipulation
root_cause: Collateral value read directly from a DEX spot price (getReserves/slot0) with no TWAP or external oracle check.
pattern: price = reserve1 * 1e18 / reserve0 (or similar) used directly as collateral valuation
preconditions: Attacker can flash-loan enough of the pooled asset to move spot price within one tx; no reentrancy guard spanning the price read and the liquidation/borrow logic.
fix: Use a TWAP oracle (Uniswap V3 observe(), or Chainlink) with sanity bounds, and/or a minimum pool liquidity check.

title: First depositor inflation attack on ERC4626-style vault
root_cause: Share price computed as totalAssets/totalSupply with no minimum initial deposit or dead shares, allowing a 1-wei deposit followed by a direct asset donation to the vault to inflate share price and round later depositors' shares to zero.
pattern: deposit() mints shares = amount * totalSupply / totalAssets without a floor/minimum liquidity burn on first deposit
preconditions: Vault is freshly deployed or has totalSupply == 0 at time of attack; attacker can transfer the underlying asset directly to the vault address.
fix: Burn a minimum number of shares to address(0) on first deposit (as OpenZeppelin ERC4626 does), or use virtual shares/assets offsetting.

title: Cross-function reentrancy via ERC777/ERC1155 callback during swap
root_cause: State (reserves) updated after external call (token transfer) rather than before, and no reentrancy guard on a second entry-point function that reads the same state.
pattern: external call (transfer/transferFrom/safeTransferFrom) happens before reserve/accounting state is written, and a sibling function lacking its own guard reads that state
preconditions: Pool accepts a token with transfer hooks (ERC777, ERC1155, or an NFT with onERC721Received), attacker re-enters via the hook into a different public function.
fix: Checks-Effects-Interactions ordering, and a reentrancy guard shared across every state-touching external function, not just the obvious one.

title: Cross-chain message replay due to missing chain-id/nonce binding
root_cause: Signed message hash does not include destination chain id or a per-chain nonce, so a valid message on chain A can be replayed verbatim on chain B or re-processed after a fork.
pattern: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(sender, amount, nonce)) with no block.chainid and a nonce that is not strictly scoped per destination chain
preconditions: Same contract/bytecode deployed on multiple chains with the same validator set or signer keys.
fix: Include block.chainid (or an explicit destination chain id) and a monotonically increasing, chain-scoped nonce in every signed payload; reject on replay via a processed-message mapping.

title: Reward-per-token rounding allows reward griefing via tiny stakes
root_cause: rewardPerTokenStored updated using integer division that truncates to zero when totalStaked is large relative to the reward rate, letting an attacker stake a dust amount to freeze reward accrual for everyone.
pattern: rewardPerToken += (rewardRate * dt * 1e18) / totalStaked computed with insufficient scaling, truncating on small totalStaked or large totalStaked edge cases
preconditions: Attacker can call stake()/withdraw() cheaply and repeatedly, or totalStaked can be pushed to an extreme value.
fix: Increase fixed-point scaling factor, and/or accrue rewards on a per-user checkpoint basis immune to global truncation.
